recipes.name: Mexican Street Corn Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (15.25 ounce) cans whole kernel corn, undrained
2 tablespoons lime juice, or to taste
1 pinch ground red pepper to taste

steps.text: Add corn with liquid to a saucepan; bring to a boil over high heat and simmer until hot. Drain; return corn to the saucepan.
Stir in cotija cheese, mayonnaise, lime juice, butter, and chili powder; transfer to a serving dish and garnish with cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Street Corn Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican street corn salad recipe is made with canned corn, butter, mayonnaise, cotija cheese, chili powder, and lime for delicious elote flavors.

review.reviewBody: Just had this. Great flavor combo. I altered the construction in that I layered the mayo, then cheese, and lastly hot sauce (instead of ground red pepper) on top of the seasoned corn. Didn't miss the butter. Also made this flavor combo using stove top cooked corn on the cob, rolling the cob in mayo (just enough sticks) then sprinkle on the cheese and sauce.

I used frozen corn and browned it a bit in the butter in a non stick pan. (Used more butter than recipe calls for). Added remaining ingredients except cilantro (because a family member dislikes it). 

Lots of compliments given and second helpings taken...and a request to make it again for an upcoming potluck.

I served it as a side fish for tacos and my son added some to his taco and said it was good like that too.

I had no trouble finding the cheese. Most grocery stores have a small refrigerated unit in their Mexican foods section. I found both grated and block cotijo there. I chose the grated...it looked like coarse parmesan. I was generous with the amount I used in the recipe but careful not to overdo it as the original poster suggested.

Five stars and this one goes into "Favorites" in my recipe book.

I didn't have any cojita cheese, so I used Parmesan instead. I used red pepper flakes instead of chili powder. It tasted so good. I will probably never serve corn with just butter, salt and pepper again. This will now be the only way to eat it. Next time I'll use mexicorn or just add some red peppers and green chilies. UPDATE: I made it again, but I roasted the corn on the stove for about 8 minutes on medium high in the butter and added some red pepper flakes. When it was done, I added the mayo and cheese and a dash of Tajin on top since I didn't have lime juice or chili powder. Delicious!

The only thing that was missing was the cob! My family loved it! I modified it a little - added 1/4 tsp seasoned salt, 3 pinches of red pepper, extra 1/2 tbsp of lime juice, extra tbsp of butter and I split the cotija cheese to be half cooked in the corn and half as topping when serving the dish. It was amazing!

This is delicious! I made it for a Memorial Day family gathering, and everyone really liked it. Only changes: I finely chopped about 1/4 cup cilantro and finely sliced 2 green onions, and mixed them into the corn. Used 3 cans of corn, one of which was the fire-roasted style. Due to more corn, I upped the cotija cheese, mayo and lime juice. Added about 1/2 tsp red chili flakes. Oh my so good!

So delicious and so easy! Followed the directions but made a few adjustments. First of all I agree with other reviewers that 2 cans does not equal 8 people. We did about eight cans and that fed 10 people. We also used only one tablespoon of butter for all 8 cans of corn and still tasted delicious! Used grated parmesan cheese as it easily mixed in with the corn, we used way less lime juice only about 2 tablespoons for the entire recipe. We also added a little bit more spice with paprika and Mexican chili powder to taste. Will definitely use this again I love corn on the cob, but this is an easier appetizer to bring with you.

Just tried this recipe and it was dee-lish!!! Seriously? Some people didn't care for this? Bland? Are we following the same recipe?! 
This tastes like authentic Mexican street corn. I used canned corn because that's all I had on hand, tapatio hot sauce, cotiga cheese, half of a fresh squeezed lime, mayo and butter in the same amounts that the recipe called for and a wee bit of garlic powder (as I love my garlic powder on corn.) My kids even loved it. Rich and yummy. You can't go wrong! I blackened my corn a little bit before I added all of the other ingredients. I'll be making again and again! Thanks!
Very good but better cold and topped with Tajin!
Simple but very tasty! I made this with frozen corn and steamed it. I tried it cold but definitely prefer it hot.

Where are the Mexican seasonings?! I made it but used the recipe as a general guide, as a starting point - added short cut green beans to the corn. Removed from the pan, then used the butter to Sauté coarsely chopped onions, adding 2 pinches of chili powder, 1tsp each of ground cumin and coriander. Sautéed until fragrant for a flavor boost then added the corn back into the saucepan. Stirred to mix all and cooked 5 mins more over medium heat to steam all ingredients. Much more characteristic of Mexican cooking 😊

Easy to make. I made half a portion. Tasted great. I used Queso Fresca for cheese, next time I'll use more. I'll probably use more cheese and spice it up a bit. (I have to be a bit careful of that, since I cook for Mom).
I added some finely chopped red onion for a little seasoning and texture.
My family LOVED it. No leftovers. Very easy recipe.
Easy but needs a little more flavor. Maybe try fire-roasted corn. Prepared in advance-would do this again but add the cheese right before serving

I didn’t bother to heat the canned corn in its own liquid and then drain. I just put the butter in the pan first, followed by the rest of the ingredients. I added ground pepper and Kosher salt. Very good!
It was my first time making it and all I can say is that this recipe is going to be one of my favorites that I intend to be making more often and share it with my friends and family : )
Not very flavorful. Cotija makes the corn have a grainy texture. Not a fan of this one.
First time making it to serve with my chicken fahitas( also made for the first time) and it was a high hit! Even my hubby ate some and he hates corn! Definitely a keeper!
